text.brief: In April 2012 the blind lawyer Chen Guangcheng climbed the wall of his farmhouse in Shandong and slipped past the guards who had held him since 2010.
text.record: Chen had exposed forced abortions and sterilizations in Linyi in 2005 and served more than four years in prison ([CECC hearing record, 2012: Chen Guangcheng](https://www.cecc.gov/sites/evo-subsites/cecc.house.gov/files/documents/hearings/2012/CECC%20Hearing%20-%20Recent%20Developments%20and%20History%20of%20the%20Chen%20Guangcheng%20Case%20-%205.3.12.pdf); [CRS report R42554: U.S.-China diplomacy over Chinese legal advocate Chen Guangcheng (May 29, 2012)](https://www.congress.gov/crs_external_products/R/PDF/R42554/R42554.5.pdf)). Friends drove him to Beijing, and American diplomats brought him into the embassy on April 26 ([State Department background briefing on Chen Guangcheng, May 2012](https://2009-2017.state.gov/p/eap/rls/rm/2012/05/182850.htm); [CRS report R42554 (May 29, 2012)](https://www.congress.gov/crs_external_products/R/PDF/R42554/R42554.5.pdf)). He left on May 2 under a deal that let him study law on the mainland, and within hours he said he feared for his family and wanted to leave ([State Department background briefing on Chen Guangcheng, May 2012](https://2009-2017.state.gov/p/eap/rls/rm/2012/05/182850.htm); [CRS report R42554 (May 29, 2012)](https://www.congress.gov/crs_external_products/R/PDF/R42554/R42554.5.pdf)). The Party let him fly to New York on May 19 ([CRS report R42554 (May 29, 2012)](https://www.congress.gov/crs_external_products/R/PDF/R42554/R42554.5.pdf)).
text.reading: The embassy's first deal rested on the Party's word, and it held only because Chen changed his mind and Washington changed with him. A local court later jailed his nephew while officials harassed his relatives, which is Stratagem 10 read to the end.
text.gapText: Architecture Principles. The embassy negotiated a protected man's future on the word of the government that had jailed and beaten him.
text.fix: Never trade a protected person's safety for assurances from the government that persecuted him, and let the person decide with full information.
